professional_sources.title: Law Society of Ontario: Generative AI, Your professional obligations
professional_sources.findings: Independent human verification before reliance; professional judgment remains with licensee; protect confidential information; context-dependent disclosure; licensee supervision and responsibility; reasonable/disclosed fees; passed-through AI disbursements actual cost.

professional_sources.title: Law Society of Ontario: Licensee use of generative artificial intelligence
professional_sources.findings: Work must meet professional competence; technological assistance does not replace active independent legal judgment. Hourly fees reflect actual time; fair/reasonable alternative fee arrangements may be considered.

professional_sources.title: Legal Aid Ontario: 2026 update to Lawyer Self-Report, AI compliance confirmation
professional_sources.findings: From January 2026 LAO roster lawyers annually confirm compliance with referenced LSO AI resources. This supports continuing relevance of the resources but is not a rule applicable to every NDA matter.

scope_mismatch_controls: Do not compare an unreviewed factual packet with counsel-led legal advice, redlining or liability-bearing engagement.
A lawyer-service listing does not prove the workflow is human-only; record tool use as unknown.
Do not average incommensurable page limits and services into a market median.
Do not infer recurring paid demand for this particular packet from advertised retail fees.
Do not use zero qualified-review time or zero acquisition/onboarding cost as the primary commercial case.
Do not call factual synthetic fixture acceptance professional legal acceptance.
recommended_scope: Reuse frozen legal lane for synthetic production measurements; retain as a serious but commercially gated portfolio finalist. Model counsel-support using transparent human-task hours x sourced rate plus equivalent supervision, or model a complete qualified-lawyer engagement only when actually supplied and verified.
